title: A graph IR separate from the parser: Java-built scene graphs and GroupBuilder stop emitting PythonParser AST nodes
description:
Repo plan merge 3B.11. PythonParser.ParsedNode (:278), NodeReference (:313) and FunctionDef (:341) are both the AST and the graph IR: GroupBuilder emits List<PythonParser.ParsedNode> (GroupBuilder.java:19), ModelScene.sceneGraph() returns it (ModelScene.java:386), GraphNodeContext stores FunctionDef group/body (:40-43). Java-built graphs therefore depend on the DSL parser. Introduce a graph program representation that the parser lowers to and GroupBuilder/sceneGraph build directly. High risk: about 230 main and 95 test files touch these types; do it after the runtime cleanup, in steps that each keep the suite green.

Rulings that apply (user, 2026-10-17): no class renames where avoidable (classes move package and keep their names; Camera stays the parent of Camera2D/Camera3D; MeshNode keeps its name); scenes and tools keep declaring their controls in a method mapping keys to functions; Palettes is the colour class patch colours merge into. Full plan and evidence: $REPO_HOME/ai-workspace/reports/repo-plan-2026-10-17.md.

DESIGN RULED (user, 2026-10-18), option C, no new IR types: the runtime's existing types ARE the graph program. MeshNode instances held in GraphNodeContext with their wired inputs/inputSources are the nodes; NodeGroup is the group (for DSL groups as well as compiled ones); InputPort/OutputPort and the recorded sources are the ports and wiring. PythonParser's nested ParsedNode, NodeReference, FunctionDef and FunctionParam stay as parser syntax only, used by the parser, the loader that turns a parse into a GraphNodeContext tree, and the source tools that rewrite .dsl text (RingDslWriter, RingTool's source edits, CollectionManifest). Two leaks to remove: (1) GroupBuilder and ModelScene.sceneGraph() build runtime objects (NodeGroup and wired nodes) directly instead of emitting ParsedNodes; (2) the runtime stops keeping syntax as its program: root.body goes, and re-evaluation order, pre-run wiring, statementAt(path), overrides and pull work on the GraphNodeContext tree. DSL groups and compiled groups run through one path (GraphNodeContext no longer stores a FunctionDef).
definition-of-done:
1. (Replaces the original item 1.) Nothing outside nodegraph.syntax, the DSL loader and the source tools (RingDslWriter, RingTool's source edits, CollectionManifest) references ParsedNode, NodeReference, FunctionDef or FunctionParam; GroupBuilder and ModelScene.sceneGraph() build NodeGroup/MeshNode wiring directly; the runtime holds no parse statements (no root.body); DSL groups and compiled groups evaluate through one path.
2. Every DSL in dsl/ and dsl/fixtures evaluates byte-identically (fingerprints); node-inspect paths and model --set overrides behave as before; ring, dungeon and quad-suite fingerprints unchanged.
3. No new IR types; class names unchanged.
4. Unit suite passes; launch entry and screenshot.
testing-plan:
1. Fingerprint every tracked DSL before and after (on tmp copies).
2. mvn test.
changes-made:
PLAN (option C, agent 2026-10-18; baseline taken first in tmp/dsl51-*-base.*: 40 DSL fingerprints identical to dsl-52's run, ring/dungeon/quad-layout node-inspect captured).
Program = a NodeGroup. NodeGraphRuntime(NodeGroup program[, groups]) holds `program` and a group table `groups` (name -> Supplier<? extends MeshNode>, replacing functionDefs). reset() makes a fresh root record and calls program.build(new GroupBuilder(this, root)), so every run gets a freshly built, pre-wired GraphNodeContext tree with fresh node instances (as today's per-run supplier.get()). No root.body.
GraphNodeContext loses `group` (FunctionDef) and `body` (List<ParsedNode>); gains `declared` (the scope's records in declaration order, evaluated or not; `children` stays the evaluated ones in evaluation order, so node-inspect order is unchanged), `inputSourcePorts`, `outputWires`/`outputWirePorts` (a group's wired outputs) and `outputSourcePorts`. A wire is a source record plus a port name in the parallel map (house rule: rows as parallel maps on the owner, no pair type): inputSources[port] = source record or literal, inputSourcePorts[port] = its port. Wiring is set at build in inputSources (a HashMap, so arguments resolve in the same order the parser's argument HashMap gave); an override replaces it with the literal at evaluation, as today; the tree is rebuilt per run. Recorded outputSources stay filled on read, as today. A source that is the reader or encloses it is a group parameter (read from its inputs), as DslGraphLayout already assumes. node.record.input(port, literal) / input(port, source, sourcePort) wire a record.
GroupBuilder(runtime, scope) builds records under scope: node(id, supplier) / node(id, type) return the GraphNodeContext; a NodeGroup node's body is built at once under it (depth capped at MAX_GROUP_DEPTH); output(name, source, port) / output(name, literal) set the scope's outputWires; `scope` is how a body reads a parameter: .input(GEOMETRY, group.scope, GEOMETRY). Type lookup order as today: runtime groups, registered nodes, library. NodeGroup gets empty default inputs()/outputs() so a program (sceneGraph, QuadLayoutNode.overSceneModel()) is an anonymous NodeGroup; build() is now called once per call record per run.
One evaluation path: a record whose node is a NodeGroup (DSL or compiled) binds defaults from node.inputs(), evaluates its declared body when whole groups run, and reads outputs through outputWires, the last-body-node rule when it wires none, and node.evaluate for declared unwired outputs (compiled groups). statementAt(path) returns the declared record; overrides, staticPorts, nearest-path suggestions and pull walk `declared`.
DSL loader = GroupLibrary (the only runtime-package class that touches syntax): parses source, turns each FunctionDef into an anonymous NodeGroup (inputs from params typed by PortType name; outputs untyped, i.e. none declared) whose build replays the body onto the GroupBuilder, resolving each NodeReference / bare name with today's scoping rules into wires; NodeGraphRuntime.fromSource/fromResource delegate to it. Reference/type errors move from mid-run to load (same messages).
Source tools keep syntax and parse the text themselves, never the runtime: RingDslWriter, RingTool's source edits, CollectionManifest, and (judgement call, flagged) GraphValidator/GraphAnalyzer/Input+LiteralParameterDescriptor/ValidateDsl/BatchDslEvaluator/SkeletonSensitivityAnalyzer, which analyse DSL text with line numbers and hand the parse to the loader to run. Run readers move to records: NodeInspector, DslGraphLayout/View, DungeonViewerScene, RingTool's graph adoption, ModelScene, MeshNodeViewerScene, MeshBooleanScene. executeGraph* drop the statements argument (the runtime runs its own program); lastId() names the program's last top-level node. ModelScene.sceneGraph() returns NodeGroup.
Behaviour changes only on invalid DSL: a param read as param.port reads the value whatever the port; an unwired port of a group is computed only when the group declares it; a DSL group call's record now holds its NodeGroup (test updated).
Steps: (1) runtime/GroupBuilder/GroupLibrary/GraphNodeContext + main callers, compile; (2) tests, mvn test; (3) regression sweep vs base, launch entry, wt done.

DONE (agent 2026-10-18), option C as planned above. The runtime's program is a NodeGroup (NodeGraphRuntime.program); every run rebuilds a pre-wired GraphNodeContext tree under root via program.build(new GroupBuilder(runtime, root)); no root.body, no functionDefs, no FunctionDef on records. GraphNodeContext: group/body removed; added declared (records in declaration order), inputSourcePorts, outputWires/outputWirePorts, outputSourcePorts, input(port, literal) and input(port, source, sourcePort). GroupBuilder(runtime, scope): node(id, supplier|type) returns the record and builds a NodeGroup's body under it; output(name, source, port); scope is the parameter source. NodeGroup gets default empty inputs()/outputs(); QuadLayoutNode.overSceneModel() and every sceneGraph() return a NodeGroup. One evaluation path for DSL and compiled groups (record.node instanceof NodeGroup). statementAt/overrides/staticPorts/pull/nearest paths walk declared. GroupLibrary is the DSL loader: load(source) / load(statements, defs) turn parses into anonymous NodeGroups (param types via PortType.valueOf) and resolve references with the old scoping rules at build time. executeGraph*(statements, ...) lost the statements argument; lastId() added; executeGraph(id) and collectInputParameters/registerFunctionDefs removed (no callers). RingTool's graph adoption reads root.declared records; ValidateDsl, BatchDslEvaluator, SkeletonSensitivityAnalyzer parse the text themselves and load the parse. Syntax types remain only in nodegraph.syntax, GroupLibrary (loader), RingDslWriter, RingTool's source edits, CollectionManifest, and the source-analysis tools GraphValidator/GraphAnalyzer/Input+LiteralParameterDescriptor/ValidateDsl/BatchDslEvaluator/SkeletonSensitivityAnalyzer/Sensitivity endpoint (they analyse DSL text with line numbers; flagged for the user).
Evidence (tmp/dsl51-*): all 40 DSLs in dsl/ and dsl/fixtures fingerprint identically base vs change (dsl51-fixtures-{base,change}.txt, also identical to dsl-52's); ring fingerprints, 299 crawfish / 10 fertility regions, dungeon_2d/3d fingerprints, quad-layout timing/node-inspect tree paths, layout input/output_sources shape and the missing-path suggestion identical (dsl51-regress-*.txt); quad-suite (bolt fertility block fandisk rockerarm hand) signatures and screenshot hashes identical, wall time only. mvn test: 528 run, 0 failures. Launch entry 'DSL-51: quad-layout'.
